name: Matt Pocock's Skills
description: A bundle of user-invoked and model-invoked agent skills covering alignment, domain modelling, TDD feedback loops, and architecture refinement.

description.value: "Skills for Real Engineers" — a bundle of small, composable agent skills (grilling/alignment, spec and ticket flows, TDD, code review, domain modelling, architecture refinement) that deliberately does not own the process, positioned against process-owning frameworks like GSD, BMAD and Spec-Kit.
description.comment: README: "These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model."

website.comment: AI Hero hosts a landing page grouping the skills (Getting Started, The Main Flow, Shaping, Upkeep, Non-Coding, Reference) plus one human-facing docs page per skill at aihero.dev/skills-<skill-name>.

creator.comment: Single-author project; plugin manifest names Matt Pocock with aihero.dev as the author URL. Repo description: "Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory."

first-release.comment: Repository created 2026-02-03; first tagged release v1.0.0 followed on 2026-06-17. Checked 2026-07-29.

latest-release.comment: v1.1.0 published 2026-07-08 (checked 2026-07-29). The plugin manifest on main already reads 1.2.0, i.e. an unreleased version is in flight.

pricing-model.comment: Entirely free MIT-licensed skill files; the only commercial adjacency is the author's free newsletter and paid courses, which are not required to use the skills.

open-source.comment: MIT (OSI-approved); the skills themselves are the entire product and live in the public repo.

covered-phases.comment: Each phase has a distinct skill and artifact: discovery (/grill-me, /grill-with-docs, /research), spec (/to-spec), architecture (/codebase-design, /improve-codebase-architecture, ADRs via /domain-modeling), planning (/wayfinder map), tasks (/to-tickets), implementation (/implement), review (/code-review), testing (/tdd). No deployment or retrospective skill exists.

methodology-style.comment: Main flow is idea → /to-spec → /to-tickets → /implement, so plan-and-execute fits; the value is the engineering discipline encoded in each skill rather than a spec compiler, so not spec-centric. Not tagged strict-tdd: /implement says "Use /tdd where possible, at pre-agreed seams" rather than making tests-first a hard gate. Not tagged multi-agent: /code-review does spawn two parallel role sub-agents and /research a background agent, but the framework is not a multi-agent role orchestration.

opinionated.comment: Deliberately non-prescriptive at the framework level — README positions against GSD/BMAD/Spec-Kit "owning the process" and invites users to install only the skills they want and edit them. Individual skills (e.g. /tdd, /grilling) are strongly opinionated internally.

ceremony-level.comment: Default flow produces a spec, a ticket set with blocking edges, CONTEXT.md glossary updates and ADRs, plus a two-axis code review — real ceremony, but each step is opt-in and no formal phase gate machinery exists.

mechanization-level.comment: Skills are markdown prompts invoked as slash commands inside the host agent; the human steps from skill to skill. The only CLI tooling is the installer (npx skills / claude plugins install) and link-skills.sh. No single command runs the workflow end-to-end.

hitl-checkpoints.comment: Human alignment is the core premise: /grill-me and /grilling interview the user until shared understanding is confirmed (explicit confirmation gate added in v1.1.0), /to-tickets iterates until the user approves the breakdown, /tdd forbids writing tests at unconfirmed seams.

approval-gates.comment: /to-spec checks the proposed test seams with the user; /wayfinder resolves decision tickets one at a time with the human answering each; /to-tickets requires explicit approval of the breakdown. /implement has no approval gate before committing — it commits to the current branch after /code-review.

autonomous-e2e.comment: No runner or loop ships that goes idea-to-merge unattended; every entry point is a human-typed slash command and the grilling skills block on human answers. Ticket blocking edges do allow several agents to work the frontier in parallel, but a human still drives each session.

autonomy-level.comment: Rated on the default configuration: phase-level approvals plus intensive question-by-question human interviewing during grilling puts it below a plain phase-gated 3. /implement runs a longer stretch autonomously once the tickets are agreed.

rollback-support.comment: No built-in undo of generated artifacts or code; recovery is plain git. /resolving-merge-conflicts explicitly works a conflict forward and never runs --abort.

supported-agents.comment: First-party metadata exists for exactly two harnesses: Claude Code (official marketplace plugin, disable-model-invocation frontmatter) and Codex (an agents/openai.yaml beside every SKILL.md). The remaining agents come from the generic `npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills` installer on skills.sh, which targets Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini, Cline and others; 'other' covers Gemini and the rest, which have no tag id.

editor-integrations.comment: The skills have no editor surface of their own — they inherit the host agent's. Primary hosts are terminal agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI); Cursor and Copilot installs via skills.sh give a VS Code-derived surface.

model-agnostic.comment: README states plainly: "They work with any model." The skills are model-neutral markdown; only the invocation metadata is harness-specific.

mcp-support.comment: No MCP server is shipped or required; the plugin manifest lists only skills. Skills shell out to the `gh` / `glab` CLIs for issue-tracker work rather than an MCP integration.

artifact-formats.comment: All produced artifacts (CONTEXT.md, ADRs, docs/agents/*.md, specs, tickets, handoff and research notes) are markdown. One exception has no tag in the schema: /improve-codebase-architecture renders its findings as a visual HTML report (there is no `html` tag id, and it is a transient report rather than a tracked artifact).

artifacts-covered.comment: specs via /to-spec, tasks via /to-tickets (tracer-bullet tickets with blocking edges), plans via the /wayfinder map, decisions as ADRs under docs/adr/, architecture via CONTEXT.md domain model plus /codebase-design and /improve-codebase-architecture. Test seams are recorded inside the spec's "Testing Decisions" section rather than as a separate test plan, so test-plans is not tagged.

project-layout.value: CONTEXT.md (or CONTEXT-MAP.md for monorepos) and docs/adr/ at the repo root; per-repo skill config in docs/agents/ (issue-tracker.md, domain.md, triage-labels.md) plus an "## Agent skills" block in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md; tickets live in GitHub/GitLab Issues or as local markdown under .scratch/<feature>/. Skills themselves install into the host agent's skill directory (e.g. ~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills).
project-layout.comment: Layout is established by the one-off /setup-matt-pocock-skills run, which explores the repo and confirms choices before writing.

artifacts-in-git.comment: CONTEXT.md, ADRs, docs/agents/ config and (in local-tracker mode) tickets under .scratch/ are all in-repo files. Tickets are out-of-repo when the configured tracker is GitHub, GitLab, or another hosted tracker.

language-agnostic.comment: Skill content is stack-neutral discipline (seams, red-green loop, Fowler smells, deep modules). Examples and the author's background lean TypeScript/JS, and one in-progress skill (setup-ts-deep-modules) is TypeScript-specific, but nothing in the promoted set requires a particular language.

enforcement-mechanisms.comment: Enforcement is overwhelmingly instructional (prompt language in SKILL.md). /code-review adds genuine agent-review via two parallel sub-agents (Standards axis with a Fowler smell baseline, Spec axis). manual-approval covers the grilling confirmation gate and ticket-breakdown sign-off. No hooks, linters, or CI checks ship with the bundle; /implement running the test suite is instruction, not a mechanical gate.

strict-phase-ordering.comment: Skills are composable and individually invocable; /ask-matt is a router that suggests which skill fits rather than a gate. The only ordering requirement is running /setup-matt-pocock-skills once before the engineering skills, and other skills merely prompt you to run it if config is missing.

artifact-validation.comment: Artifacts follow prose templates (spec template, ADR format, CONTEXT format) with no schema check. The `claude plugin validate` step in the repo's own CLAUDE.md validates the plugin manifests, not user-produced artifacts.

memory-implementation.comment: Persistent context is CONTEXT.md (shared domain language), docs/adr/ decisions, docs/agents/ config, and /handoff documents. The issue tracker doubles as long-horizon memory for /wayfinder maps, but no database or vector store is involved.

persistent-memory.comment: In-repo CONTEXT.md/ADRs are read at the start of exploration in later sessions, and /wayfinder is explicitly built for work "more than one agent session can hold", carrying state on the tracker. /handoff exists for the cases where a manual compaction is still wanted.

project-context-files.comment: /setup-matt-pocock-skills writes an "## Agent skills" section into the repo's existing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md (never creating a second one) and produces CONTEXT.md plus docs/agents/*.md.

cost-tracking.comment: The bundle tracks no tokens or cost; any reporting comes from the host agent. Token frugality is a stated design goal (the shared CONTEXT.md language is pitched as reducing thinking tokens), but nothing measures it.

run-history.comment: No structured run log or trace store. The closest analogues are human-readable and manual: /handoff documents, /research output files, and closed wayfinder tickets on the issue tracker.

telemetry-opt.comment: The bundle collects no telemetry of its own — it is plain markdown skill files with no runtime — so the user has full control by absence of collection. (The skills.sh registry publishes install counts for its own distribution, which is outside the repo.)

custom-templates.comment: The skills.sh install path deliberately writes editable files you own ("Hack around with them. Make them your own."), and /writing-great-skills is a reference for authoring your own. The Claude Code plugin path is read-only and managed by contrast.

hooks.comment: No lifecycle hook system; the plugin manifest ships skills only. The repo contains a couple of shell templates (diagnosing-bugs/scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh, scripts/link-skills.sh) but these are helper scripts, not user-registered pre/post-phase hooks.

sub-agents.comment: The whole product is user-definable skills, with a documented user-invoked vs model-invoked contract and a /writing-great-skills reference. Shipped skills also delegate to sub-agents (/code-review's two parallel reviewers, /research's background agent).

marketplace.comment: Distributed through Claude Code's official plugin marketplace (the repo is also its own single-plugin marketplace via .claude-plugin/marketplace.json) and listed on the skills.sh community registry alongside other authors' skill packs.

install-mechanism.comment: `npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills` (npm) copies editable skill files in; cloning plus scripts/link-skills.sh symlinks them by hand. The third path, `claude plugins install mattpocock-skills`, is an agent plugin manager with no matching tag id in the schema (editor-extension would be a stretch — Claude Code is a CLI agent, not an editor extension).

setup-time.comment: README titles the section "Installation (30-second setup)": one install command plus one /setup-matt-pocock-skills run per repo, which asks about issue tracker, triage labels, and doc layout.

self-hosted.comment: Skills are local markdown files executed by a locally-running agent; no hosted service is part of the workflow.

requires-account.comment: No account is required for the skills themselves (the newsletter is optional). You do need a subscription to whatever coding agent hosts them, and the default GitHub/GitLab issue-tracker mode needs an authenticated gh/glab CLI — local-markdown tracking avoids even that.

git-worktree-support.comment: No mention of git worktrees in the README or in the skills reviewed (to-tickets, implement, code-review, wayfinder, setup). Parallelism is expressed as tickets with blocking edges that several agents can pick up, leaving isolation to the user.

documentation-quality.comment: Long, example-rich README organised around four named failure modes; a per-skill human-facing docs page on aihero.dev; every skill self-documents in its SKILL.md; the repo publishes its own ADRs, an invocation contract, and a changeset-driven CHANGELOG.

github-stars.comment: 194,114 stars and 16,708 forks as of 2026-07-29 — extremely fast growth for a repo created 2026-02-03. Stales quickly.

active-maintenance.comment: Latest commit 2026-07-28 and a push on 2026-07-29, well inside the 90-day window; v1.1.0 shipped 2026-07-08 with v1.2.0 already staged in the plugin manifest.

example-projects.comment: Weak-to-moderate: the README links a real CONTEXT.md from the author's course-video-manager repo as a worked example and the aihero.dev hub links write-ups on daily use, but there is no dedicated sample project or third-party case study.

community-channel.comment: GitHub Discussions is enabled on the repo (with ~248 open issues as an active feedback surface). The main announcement channel is the author's ~60,000-subscriber newsletter, which has no tag id in the schema; no Discord or Slack is advertised in the repo.
